commits_info.message:
2.16.0 release (previous 2.15.6) + release notes updated by CI build 3257

[ci skip-release]

Merge pull request #1321 from moltmann/KeepWeakRefsInInvocations

Prevent memory leaks with inline MockMakers by using weak refs to mocks

[ci maven-central-release]

Bumped minor version

We haven't had a Maven Central release in a month, let's bump a minor version and push new version to Central.

Using MockWeakReference instead of WeakReference

This way we communicate the intent more clearly and we have better error reporting.

Package cleanup

Avoided importing classes from "org.mockito.internal.creation.bytebuddy" in other parts of the code. It is needed to isolate bytebuddy dependency.
Reduced the public API of MockWeakReference

Removed unnecessary serialVersionUID

We don't use it consistently in the code.

Reduced complexity

We don't need the conditional logic. We can use the caller to decide what MockReference to pass.

Renamed classes

MockReference communicates the intent more clearly than SerializableReference
Tweaked exception message and added coverage

Coverage for inline memory leaking of serializable mocks

I noticed that we're missing some test coverage. We added code to handle serializable mocks with weak references. I verified that this test fails if we remove weak references from serializable mocks.

Made java memory setting local to the project that needs it

Also updated comments

Fixes #1313: Use weak refs to mock in invocations

This is needed for mock makers that store a
map<weakref<mock>, invocation>. If the invocation holds a strong
reference to the mock, the key never gets gc-ed and the map keeps on
growing.

As weak reference cannot be serialized, temporarily create a strong
reference during serialization.

As the tests use invocations without keeping references to the mock we
need to keep strong references in these cases.
